content: The Codex quota footer uses ModelRegistry.getApiKeyForProvider plus readStoredCredential because Pi 0.80.8 removed extension access to ModelRegistry.authStorage.
pi-tools extension settings will support manually edited global and trusted project config files plus an in-Pi management command/UI.
The `/pi-tools` configuration UI should render every setting registered by pi-tools extensions from the initial implementation.
Remove the legacy `/codex-quota` shortcut; footer quota settings are managed exclusively through the unified `/pi-tools` interface and shared config.
Pi loads each extension with an isolated module cache, so settings definitions are synchronized to the `/pi-tools` manager through Pi's shared event bus rather than a shared module-level registry.
`/pi-tools` persists each edit immediately but defers extension reload until the settings UI closes, allowing batch edits without reopening the UI.
Tool-output compression defaults to observe; any profile must be explicitly set to apply before it can store raw output and replace a result.
Tool-output compression will use a single private SQLite store with WAL, `synchronous=FULL`, and serialized write-safe multi-instance transactions rather than separate artifact files and an index.

Compression will start as a result-side exact-duplicate-reuse foundation without permanently excluding future techniques; apply behavior is configured by tool scope rather than per-result user approval, and retrieval is an agent tool rather than a user workflow.
Stored tool-output references are retrievable only by the session that created them, and retrieval is limited to UTF-8-safe chunks no larger than 48 KiB.

Apply mode stores the first eligible text result unchanged and replaces only a later same-session byte-identical result when its committed retrieval reference saves at least 16 bytes; all uncertainty fails open.
Future compression work will use aggregate usage data and agent assistance to propose trusted-project output profiles, but every profile requires explicit human review and enablement.

The Go test profile defaults to observe via `profiles.test.go.mode`, aggregates successful normal or verbose package summaries with verbose passing detail raw-only after durable storage, and leaves failed, malformed, composite, or never-worse results unchanged.

Tool-output compression uses a generic profile registry with category-aligned profiles.<category>.<profile>.mode settings and no compatibility aliases or migrations for unreleased profile architecture.
Implement the safe generic bash JSON/JSONL profile despite modest local corpus savings because other workflows may emit substantially more structured output.
